Hard constraints that drive plot: L146 'I can't arrest a village.', L194 'Jaina couldn't tell a drilled man's walk from a tired one', L208 'I won't know who put it there.', L334 'see nothing in the groove but good grain' (this sets up why Havel's spike-at-the-gate plan at L400 fails), L394 'Kett keeps nothing overnight.', L436 'They don't talk,', L438 'he can't bite down on anything' / 'I can only do it once tonight', L456 'The inspection office's tag won't open it, but I know the kind of lock'. Binary diagnostics acted on in scene: L104 'Damp doesn't stop at a street corner. This does.', L124 'It isn't four yards', L240 'You'll get nothing there tonight, and you'll get Fenner's crew', L275 'had nothing to hide, or had somebody else to do his looking for him' (she looks up because of it), L317 'no mask at all' / 'came no nearer the sacks than that' (the evidence for L319's two kinds of men), L330 'If he had seen her, he would not stand at the window like that' (the next line, 'Unless...', complicates it), L396 'I'd not call that nothing.' Self-argument in free indirect thought: L24 'Nobody could order a man's nib to chatter...', L402 'She had no better reason to doubt him than...' / 'It wasn't fair, and she kept it anyway.' Spatial precision or tactical absence inventory: L224 'couldn't see a stride into any of them', L236 'Nobody she couldn't account for.', L297 'no wagon, no doorway deep enough to stand in, no turning' (no 'but Z' landing; the missing cover is why she goes up on the roofs). The keep rate is above 20%, so every keep was rechecked against the adversarial self-check. None of the 27 has the not-X-then-Y shape. Each one states a limit, a piece of evidence or a binary choice that the scene acts on. No pivot rhythm repeats anywhere in the chapter.

findings.text: The ordinance sends a notice to the gate post whenever an inspector flags a shipment, so I bring them here myself.
findings.pattern: intent-smear P10 (receiver noun doing the human work / actor demoted)
findings.subject: the ordinance
findings.realAgent: the inspector who flags the shipment (and Corin, who carries the notices himself, as the same sentence admits)
findings.reason: A law is given the physical act of sending while the people who actually send and carry the notice sit in a subordinate clause. With the inspector put back as subject the meaning is unchanged, so the actor was demoted.
findings.suggestedFix: When an inspector flags a shipment, he has to send a notice to the gate post. I bring them here myself.

findings.text: Every flagged load leaves a bag in the sample room.
findings.pattern: intent-smear P10 (receiver noun doing the human work / actor demoted)
findings.subject: every flagged load
findings.realAgent: the inspector or office clerk who draws and seals the sample bag
findings.reason: The load is given the act of depositing a sealed, labelled sample, work a person does. This was borderline on its own, but it sits between the L130 and L180 KILLs in the same stretch of Corin's speech, so the cluster rule ('A KEEP that appears near 2+ KILLs -> downgrade to KILL') makes it a KILL.
findings.suggestedFix: The inspector takes a bag off every flagged load for the sample room.

findings.text: The sample room wants a magister's ring on the door.
findings.subject: the sample room
findings.realAgent: the door's lock, which opens only to a magister's ring (the magisters who set that rule)
findings.reason: A room is given desire ('wants'), which matches the calibration example 'the city wanted something from her'. The real constraint is a lock and the person who holds the ring. The fix avoids the narration's wording at L194 ('a door that opened to a magister's ring') so it doesn't create an echo.
findings.suggestedFix: You need a magister's ring for the sample room door.

findings.text: Sylvanas looked at him: the ink, the satchel, the bruised eyes. Then she pulled her knife out of the table
findings.reason: This is the fifth reaction or assessment eye beat in the chapter, one over the cap of 4, and it is the weakest of the five: a generic look-before-verdict that re-lists Corin's established tags (ink, satchel, bruised eyes) and adds nothing. Her decision is carried by the next line, 'Stay behind Proudmoore'. L54's stand-off has the dried blood, L80 shows Havel clocking the bows, L162 is Jaina's fatigue waking to attention, and L370 makes the crock-to-'Heavy' link visible without narration, so each of those does more work.
